full_judgment:
4. The petitioner alleges in the writ petition that the impugned order has been passed without issuing any prior notice to show cause upon the petitioner which is violative of section 32 of the Customs Act 1969 as well as the fundamental rights guaranteed under the constitution. Further case of the petitioner is that the impugned letter of demand dated 24.12.96 is also illegal as the same has been issued beyond the period of limitation of 3 years as contemplated in section 32(2) of the Customs Act 1969. 

 11. But the fact remains that prior notice, provided under Section 32(2) of the Customs Act having not been served and the impugned order having been issued much beyond the period of 3 years limitation, the question of exhausting the alternative forum is not sustainable as the provision of law has not been complied with. Mr. Khan, the learned. Counsel in this respect referred to the case of Rahman Food Corporation Ltd. Vs. Deputy Collector of Customs & ors. reported in 49 DLR(HCD) 510. In Paragraph 12 and 14 of the said decision their Lordships held inter alia as follows: 

 15. So in our view non issuance of the notice upon the petitioner as provided under section 32(2) of the Customs Act 1969 is beyond the principle of law and also against the principle of natural justice and the impugned demand dated 24.12.96 being made beyond the period of limitation, the same is liable to be declared to have been issued illegally and as such liable to be cancelled.
